title: Efficient Estimation of Reduced QAOA Expressibility on Acyclic Graphs
authors: Bao Bach, Boris Tsvelikhovskiy, Jose Falla, Ilya Safro
abstract: Classically equivalent formulations of an optimization problem need not lead to equivalent quantum algorithms. For MaxCut, fixing the value of a single vertex removes a simple global symmetry without changing the underlying optimization problem, yet it can substantially alter the quantum dynamics generated by the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). These dynamics are captured by the circuit's dynamical Lie algebra (DLA), whose direct construction can become exponentially expensive. Here we show that, for symmetry-reduced QAOA on trees, substantial information about the reduced DLA can instead be obtained efficiently from the graph alone. We introduce a polynomial classical algorithm that recursively distinguishes vertices using shortest path structure and degree parity. When all vertices are resolved individually, the method determines the complete reduced DLA and, under the corresponding graph conditions, certifies maximal expressibility of the reduced QAOA ansatz. Even when full resolution is not achieved, the algorithm identifies embedded subalgebras, provides rigorous lower bounds on DLA dimension, and certifies controllable subsystems. Our theoretical and experimental results show how classical graph structure can be used to diagnose and potentially guide the quantum dynamics of variational algorithms before running them on quantum hardware.
summary: This paper introduces a polynomial classical algorithm to analyze the reduced Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA) for QAOA, specifically when applied to tree graphs. By leveraging graph structure properties like shortest paths and degree parities, the authors can determine the quantum dynamics' expressibility. This allows researchers to theoretically guide and understand quantum algorithms using only classical graph theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of determining the expressive power and controllability of quantum circuits, specifically for the QAOA algorithm, whose underlying dynamics are captured by the Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA).
main_result: For QAOA on tree graphs, the authors developed a polynomial classical algorithm that can determine the reduced DLA structure, certifying maximal expressibility or providing rigorous lower bounds on the DLA dimension.
method: The approach involves developing a classical, polynomial-time algorithm that recursively partitions graph vertices using shortest-path distances and degree parities to analyze the structure of the reduced DLA.
model_or_system: The model is the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) applied to combinatorial optimization problems like MaxCut. The dynamics are analyzed via the Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA) generated by the problem and mixer Hamiltonians.
key_observables: The structure and dimension of the reduced Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA), and the containment of single-site Pauli operators within this algebra.
important_parameters: The graph structure ($\Gamma$), particularly when it is a tree (acyclic), which simplifies the Lie-algebraic analysis.
main_assumptions: The core results are established under the assumption that the underlying graph $\Gamma$ is connected and acyclic (a tree).
figures_summary: The notes reference figures illustrating the symmetry-reduction framework (fixing a reference vertex $v$) and the general structure of the QAOA circuit.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of DLA construction to a specific, tractable case: QAOA on trees. It introduces graph-theoretic diagnostics (distance layers, parity patterns) to derive algebraic containment results for the reduced DLA.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, purely classical structural tool to diagnose the fundamental quantum limitations (expressibility) of variational quantum algorithms before running them on expensive quantum hardware.

In the presence of a global bit-flip symmetry, fixing the bit value at any chosen reference vertex v yields a reduced optimization problem equivalent to the original, along with a reduced QAOA ansatz and its corresponding reduced dynamical Lie algebra. A canonical example exhibiting this symmetry is the MaxCut problem, which serves as the primary focus of this work.
